Help nearby

Helplines

112Emergency (police, fire, ambulance)1091Women helpline (police)181Women helpline108Ambulance1930Cyber crime

Quick tools

  1. Get to a safe placeSomewhere lit with people around. Call 112 if you are in danger.
  2. Get medical careAny hospital, government or private, must give first aid and treatment free after sexual assault or an acid attack. The hospital informs the police. (BNSS section 397)
  3. Keep what could be evidenceIf you can, do not wash or change clothes before the medical check. Keep messages, call logs and screenshots.
  4. Report at any police stationAny station must register it, wherever it happened (Zero FIR). For sexual offences a woman officer records it. You can also send it online and sign within 3 days. (BNSS section 173)
  5. Ask for free help181 connects you to a One Stop Centre: shelter, counselling, medical and legal help. 15100 is the free legal aid line.
112 181 15100
